abstract: Reasoning models frequently agree with incorrect user suggestions - a behavior known as sycophancy. However, it is unclear where in the reasoning trace this agreement originates and how strong the commitment is. We introduce sycophantic anchors - sentences identified via counterfactual analysis that commit models to user agreement. Across four reasoning models spanning three architecture families (Llama, Qwen, Falcon-hybrid) and 1.5B - 8B parameters, we analyze over 200,000 counterfactual rollouts and show that linear probes reliably detect sycophantic anchors (74 - 85% balanced accuracy), outperforming text-only baselines at high commitment levels -confirming they capture internal states beyond surface vocabulary. title: Sycophantic Anchors: Localizing and Quantifying User Agreement in Reasoning Models
